newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine town on watch for Versace suspect.
newsitem.headline: Philippine town on watch for Versace suspect.

text.p: The Filipino father of suspected American serial killer Andrew Cunanan locked his house and left town on Friday as the Philippines mounted a watch for the main suspect in the murder of fashion king Gianni Versace.
His face hidden by a towel, former U.S. Navy sailor Modesto Cunanan and a female companion drove off in a car for an unknown destination, refusing to say anything.
In her house in nearby Baliuag town, an aunt of the younger Cunanan went into hysterics and screamed at media men.
"No comment, no comment. I have nothing to say, leave us in peace," Barbara Cunanan Carlos shouted.

Described by U.S. police as a male prostitute, Andrew Cunanan has been the subject of a massive hunt in the United States since Versace was gunned down outside his mansion in Miami Beach, Florida, on Tuesday.

Philippine law enforcement agencies alerted units nationwide about Cunanan on the chance the 27-year-old fugitive might turn up in the country, where his father lives in the sleepy town of Plaridel, in Bulacan province, just north of Manila.
"We cannot discount the possibility that if he flees from the U.S., he might come here," said Art Villarta, Bulacan provincial chief of the Philippine National Bureau of Investigation (NBI).
"We have nothing against him but our instructions are to monitor the whereabouts of his relatives just in case he might join them," Villarta told Reuters.

The NBI tracked down Modesto Cunanan's whereabouts after it was informed by the U.S. embassy of his postal address in the Philippines, Villarta said, adding the NBI was sure the man was the father of the American suspect.
"There's no doubt, 100 percent. It's him (Modesto) really, the father of Andrew Cunanan," Villarta said.
Born and reared in the United States, Versace's alleged killer was the son of Modesto Cunanan by his first marriage, according to Villarta.
In 1988, according to NBI records, the younger Cunanan came to the Philippines for his first and only known visit to his father's country.
Residents of the town said he buried himself in books most of the time and left an impression of a young man of good manners.

"He said he will try to go into foreign service, and I said, 'Go ahead with it because being a diplomat is just the right thing for you'," family friend Nonilo Katipunan told Manila's GMA television network.
At Manila's international airport, immigration officials posted at arrival counters newspaper photographs of Cunanan as part of the official alert.
"We have sent a directive to our airport and sea ports throughout the Philippines that he should be turned over to the NBI if he tries to enter the country," an immigration spokesman said.
"We have also directed our agents to closely scrutinise passports for any possible tampering."
Cunanan was already on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list before the Versace killing because of four murders in three states in April and May.
